order: Address two findings from review. First, creation-time identity capture must not degrade to a lexical guess: have checkout creation determine the canonical path itself and refuse the checkout, with the registration cleaned up, when that lookup fails; the lexical fallback should serve only paths that are already gone through sweeping. Pin a regression for a poisoned-real-path scenario. Second, make both review-lane kill branches poll git's actual registration lock rather than sleeping a fixed duration, since a slow checkout can remain locked past any fixed delay. Also correct the continuous-integration records: name the actual pull-request-head run rather than a generic label, and record the superseded run's true outcome, including a flake that fired during that run.
claims: Creation-time identity capture no longer degrades to a lexical guess: checkout creation determines the canonical path itself and refuses the checkout, with registration cleaned up, when that lookup fails, and a poisoned-real-path regression is pinned. Both review-lane kill branches now poll the actual registration lock instead of sleeping a fixed duration. The records were corrected to name the true pull-request-head run and the superseded run's real outcome. Suites: verifier 99, router 135, registry 31, review-lane 116 (twice), full CI-equivalent run green.
